openQuestions: Controlling court rule: expungement procedure is statutory; no dedicated court rule identified. Unresolved.

Excluded circumstances: dismissal following completion of a supervisory treatment or diversion program is treated differently and interacts with the one-time-only rules elsewhere in the chapter. Unresolved and important, because pretrial intervention and conditional discharge dismissals are common in New Jersey and the participant will describe them as dismissals.
Pending-charge restriction: a person with a pending criminal matter is generally not eligible until it is resolved; verify against 2C:52-14. Unresolved as applied to this track specifically.
Individualized legal judgment: whether the disposition was a true dismissal or acquittal, or a dismissal after diversion, which routes differently.
Individualized legal judgment: whether every count was resolved favorably, which is the gate for the expedited route.
Individualized legal judgment: whether any related charge remains open.

Output-strategy prose (review stage table): stage 1 record confirmation from the New Jersey State Police and the courts = process_guidance; stage 2 petition, statements, order for hearing and proposed expungement order = official_pdf_fill, or assembly through the Judiciary Expungement System; stage 3 filing, service, objection window, order distribution to every record-holding agency = process_guidance.

Output-strategy prose: 'New Jersey publishes a statewide Judiciary kit with standardized forms, and the Judiciary's own electronic Expungement System assembles the petition and proposed order from entered data. That makes this official_pdf_fill rather than custom_pleading. But the back end, particularly service of the signed order on every agency that holds a record, is sequencing work that no document can carry.'
Official form status: statewide-approved. The Judiciary kit forms are the paper path and the Expungement System is the electronic path.

Custom pleading: 'The statute prescribes petition contents at 2C:52-7 rather than a form, so a compliant custom pleading is legally possible. It is the wrong choice given that the Judiciary generates the documents for free.'
Process control: court-controlled, with prosecutor and agency objection rights, then agency-controlled at execution.

Venue rule: for conviction tracks the statute specifies the county of residence or a county where a conviction was adjudged; for arrest-only matters the venue rule needs separate confirmation against 2C:52-6. Unresolved. Do not repeat the internal reference's 'county of the most recent offense' formulation, which does not match the statutory language reviewed.
Local practice: New Jersey is a unified statewide court system with 15 vicinages; no local form variation identified. Unresolved whether individual vicinages impose practice requirements.

Required supporting documents: none filed as a matter of statute, but the participant needs, for every matter, the date, court, offense, complaint or indictment number, docket number, and disposition. Missing case identifiers are the leading cause of rejected petitions.
Response or objection period: agencies have a window to object; the exact period should be confirmed against 2C:52-9 through 2C:52-11 and 2C:52-10.1. Unresolved.
Continuing disclosure obligations: limited, subject to the surviving statutory uses; confirm the exact carve-outs against 2C:52-27. Unresolved.

Self-help limits listed by the review: dismissal after pretrial intervention, conditional discharge or another diversion program; prosecutor objection; any count still open; federal, out-of-state or tribal records; immigration exposure (New Jersey expungement has no federal immigration effect); the participant cannot assemble complete case identifiers.
OPEN QUESTION 1: Venue rule for arrest-only petitions under 2C:52-6. Release blocker.
OPEN QUESTION 2: Treatment of dismissals following diversion. Release blocker, because these participants will present as ordinary dismissals.
OPEN QUESTION 3: Exact objection window. Unresolved.
OPEN QUESTION 4: Current Judiciary form numbers and revisions. Build blocker.
LEGAL-DESIGN DECISION: [x] Approved for implementation with the limitations listed below.
Limitation 1: Build this track first. It is free, fast, and the expedited route can be immediate.
Limitation 2: Screen for diversion dismissals before promising anything.
Limitation 3: Service of the signed order on every record-holding agency must ship with the packet as a checklist built from the State Police history.

reviewOpenQuestions: HEADLINE FINDING 1: The disorderly persons cap is five, not four. 2C:52-3(b) permits no more than five disorderly persons offenses, five petty disorderly persons offenses, or a combination of no more than five. The internal reference says four throughout, including in its routing table and its agent guidance. This is the most consequential error in the document, because the count is what decides whether a participant goes to regular expungement or is pushed to the ten-year Clean Slate track.

HEADLINE FINDING 2: The early pathways are three years and four years, not one figure. Four years for the indictable route under 2C:52-2(a)(2); three years for the disorderly persons route under 2C:52-3(b)(2). The internal reference states four for both.

HEADLINE FINDING 3: Venue is wrong in the internal reference. The statute puts venue in the Superior Court of the county where the person resides or a county in which one or more of the convictions were adjudged. The reference says the county of the most recent offense.
HEADLINE FINDING 4: Title 39 motor vehicle offenses cannot be expunged at all under 2C:52-28, so DWI is outside expungement in New Jersey.

HEADLINE FINDING 5: New Jersey has no numeric cap on same-day or closely-related bundles. Both 2C:52-2 and 2C:52-3 carry separate routes for convictions entered on the same day and for offenses that were interdependent or closely related within a comparatively short period, and these routes are not subject to the one-crime or five-offense counts.

HEADLINE FINDING 6: The automated Clean Slate process is still not operational. 2C:52-5.4 requires the State to build it and 2C:52-5.3 closes the petition route once it exists. Assembly Bill 5095, introduced May 14, 2026, is direct evidence the automation is not in place and the 2C:52-5.3 petition remains available. This is the single most important status fact in the state and it needs a standing monitor.
HEADLINE FINDING 7: There is no court filing fee, confirmed by the Judiciary kit, which was updated in June 2020 specifically to remove it.

PART 4 - process-guidance specification is cross-cutting and applies across tracks, not a relief mechanism, so it is not an inventory entry. It fixes the controlling process and a fourteen-step sequence beginning with the NJSP SBI criminal history and ending with post-order verification allowing six to twelve months; the records the participant must obtain (NJSP SBI fingerprint-based criminal history for a fee, court records for gaps, proof of sentence completion and payment, FBI Identity History Summary where out-of-state or federal records may exist); what LegalEase can prepare; what LegalEase cannot complete (the SBI request, the Expungement System submission if the Judiciary requires the participant's own account, the prosecutor's objection decision, any hearing, and the agencies' execution of the order); and the attorney-handoff triggers.

PART 5 COMPLETENESS - one checkbox is expressly NOT satisfied: 'Relevant official forms were classified. Not satisfied. No New Jersey forms were supplied and the Judiciary kit was last confirmed updated in June 2020.' All other completeness checkboxes are marked satisfied, with the qualification that Track 8 (2C:52-5) is identified but unread and flagged as a completeness gap and has no proposed output strategy.

OVERALL JURISDICTION DECISION: [x] Approved with listed limitations. LEGAL-DESIGN DECISION: [x] Approved for implementation with limitations. The review notes the difficulty is entirely in eligibility, because New Jersey's counting rules, bundling routes, marijuana regrading provisions and non-expungeable lists interact in ways a naive engine will get wrong.

PACKET-GENERATION QUESTION: [x] Yes. New Jersey's process is built around preparing a verified petition and a proposed order that a judge signs; the Judiciary kit tells filers to leave the signature line blank for the judge and to leave the monies-owed section for the court. Two conditions attach: disclosure (which sections the court completes, that the prosecutor and named agencies may object, that the court may enter the order without a hearing if no one objects, and that the participant must serve the signed order on every record-holding agency afterwards) and restraint (every fact in the verified petition must come from the participant or an official record, and LegalEase must not assert compelling circumstances, offense grading, or eligibility conclusions that belong to the court).

Review legal-design decision quoted: '[x] Approved for implementation with the limitations listed below' — (1) this is the only real packet in New York, build it, and build the Certificate of Disposition step first because nothing else can be completed without it; (2) apply the 160.59 exclusion list, not the Clean Slate list, they differ on class A drug felonies and on violent felonies; (3) the rehabilitation showing is assisted work, not template output; (4) compare against Clean Slate before recommending a filing, since for a participant between years three or eight and year ten who is Clean Slate eligible the automatic route is faster and free, subject to the implementation backlog.
